headline: Key vault contracts verified on Etherscan; recognized auditors (Spearbit, OZ, Cantina) but no audit links pinned; proxy implementation not independently verified this run; primary source repo is private

findings.text: 0x3bd9248048df95Db4fBD748C6CD99C1bAa40bAD0 (gtUSDa MultiDepositorVault, Ethereum) is verified on Etherscan (ABI source: etherscan, no proxy). 0x2b8f37893ee713a4e9ff0ceb79f27539f20a32a1 (Morpho Prime USDC, Ethereum) is a proxy verified on Etherscan (ABI source: etherscan) pointing to implementation 0xcbe3A584180F2897dF44c9AD3Fd840f06bD283f4; the implementation contract was not independently fetched this run. Other address_book entries (0xe3ae7C, 0xF587f2, 0x74C4A6, Base/Arbitrum/Optimism vault addresses) were not individually verified this run.

A public GitHub snapshot repo exists at https://github.com/aera-finance/aera-contracts-public containing v1, v2, and v3 subdirectories. However, the primary development repo (aera-contracts-v3) is private, the public repo carries no tagged releases, and no commit SHA was pinned against deployed bytecode in this run. Source-to-repo correspondence is plausible but not confirmed.

No audit links appear in protocol.audit_links (listed as none recorded). Off-chain sources confirm: (1) Aera contracts audited by Spearbit and OpenZeppelin (referenced on aera.finance and in Gauntlet blog post dated March 2026); (2) a Cantina security competition targeting aera-v3 completed June 25, 2025 (commit 4c24979c7928dfe687e16f2cf58f6219e76103f9, private repo); (3) an active Immunefi bug bounty referenced. The Cantina competition references a prior Google Drive audit report but that URL was not opened this run. No audit PDF or report URL was independently fetched or pinned.

Named auditors Spearbit and OpenZeppelin are broadly recognized Solidity audit firms. Cantina is a recognized security competition platform. However, auditor identity is based on off-chain website claims, not from fetching a signed audit report PDF.

Post-audit drift cannot be assessed: the primary Aera v3 source repo is private (aera-contracts-v3), the Cantina competition commit (4c24979c...) is in a private repo, and the public snapshot repo (aera-contracts-public/v3) does not expose commit history with timestamps. No diff between audited commit and deployed bytecode was possible this run.

0x2b8f37893ee713a4e9ff0ceb79f27539f20a32a1 is a proxy; its implementation 0xcbe3A584180F2897dF44c9AD3Fd840f06bD283f4 was not independently fetched to verify bytecode verification status. The DeFiPunkd surfacer auto-resolved the proxy and returned an etherscan-sourced merged ABI, suggesting the implementation is also verified, but this was not independently confirmed via a direct fetch this run.

steelman.red: The primary source repo (aera-contracts-v3) is private, no audit links appear in protocol.audit_links, the proxy implementation (0xcbe3A...) was not directly verified this run, and several address_book entries were not checked — an outsider cannot independently audit the codebase.
steelman.orange: While Etherscan verification is confirmed for the two main fund-custody contracts and recognized auditors (Spearbit, OpenZeppelin, Cantina) are referenced, no audit PDFs are linked in protocol.audit_links, the implementation contract for the proxy was not independently verified this run, the primary source repo is private, and no commit SHA was pinned — partial verifiability at best.
steelman.green: Both sampled fund-custody contracts are Etherscan-verified, a public source snapshot repo exists, and multiple recognized-firm audits (Spearbit, OpenZeppelin, Cantina competition June 2025) are referenced from the official Gauntlet/Aera websites, meeting the spirit of the green criteria.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because: (1) no audit URLs appear in protocol.audit_links and no audit PDF was fetched this run, so V3 relies solely on off-chain website claims; (2) the proxy implementation 0xcbe3A... was not independently verified via direct fetch; (3) the primary Aera v3 source repo is private, preventing a source-to-repo commit match; these gaps collectively prevent a green grade even though the two sampled contracts show Etherscan verification and recognized-firm audits are credibly referenced.

protocol_metadata.about: Gauntlet is a yield curator that deploys risk-managed DeFi strategies for institutional capital allocators, fintechs, and stablecoin issuers. Users deposit stablecoins or other assets into Gauntlet-curated vaults (including the Aera-infrastructure gtUSDa cross-chain vault and Morpho-based MetaMorpho vaults) that automatically rebalance across hundreds of lending markets, chains, and protocols to optimize risk-adjusted returns. The flagship Gauntlet USD Alpha (gtUSDa) vault issues an ERC-20 receipt token and routes capital across Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and Optimism via asynchronous solver-based provisioning. Gauntlet acts as the off-chain risk manager (guardian) while the Aera smart contract infrastructure enforces on-chain guardrails.
